name: Huawei Atlas 300I Duo inference card (dual 310-series, 48/96 GB)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Primary source states the CARD-TOTAL figure: LPDDR4X, 48 GB or 96 GB, 'Total bandwidth (entire card): 408 GB/s', ECC. Per-processor bandwidth is not stated but follows as 408/2 = 204 GB/s, consistent with the single-processor cards' 204.8 GB/s. Source cn-huawei-atlas-300i-duo-spec. Note the schema records a single number per record, so the 48 GB bin is under-reported by this field and the per-card basis is stated here explicitly.
notes:
THE HIERARCHY POINT: this card is the one that shows what Huawei actually does when memory capacity and memory bandwidth come into conflict, and the answer is instructive for anyone modelling memory-bound inference: going from one 310-series processor to two on the same board exactly doubles capacity to 96 GB while leaving bandwidth essentially flat per die at ~204 GB/s. Arithmetic intensity therefore HALVES relative to the 24 GB single card. The 96 GB bin is the only way to hold a 70B-class model in FP16 on an Ascend inference card without sharding, and the price of that capacity is a worse roofline position, not a better one - the band gets wider and no more data arrives. Compare directly to a single HBM GPU part: 96 GB at 408 GB/s is roughly 4.7x less bandwidth per byte than a same-generation 80 GB HBM card. Form factor is FHFL single-slot 10.5 inches, 150 W, 910 g, PCIe Gen4 x16, same PCI ID base (0x19E5:0xD500) with a different subsystem device ID (0x0110 vs 0x0100 on the Pro), which is a useful confirmation that these are the same NPU in a different packaging. Codec: 256-channel 1080p30 decode (or 32x 4K60), 48-channel 1080p30 encode, 4K JPEG at 1024 FPS decode. Also splits into up to 7 virtual NPUs per processor, so 14 virtual instances on one card. A community-comparative Llama 3 measurement (~150 tok/s at 96 GB versus ~220 tok/s for an RTX 4090) is the only public throughput datapoint I could find for this silicon; it is a hobbyist report, not a benchmark, and is not recorded as a benchmark record.
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). %s NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH. That is the standing rule for this field in this repo and it was applied to every null here rather than to a subset: a width derived by dividing a published aggregate bandwidth by an assumed or half-assumed per-pin rate is two inferences stacked on one number, and if either inference is wrong the record looks populated while being wrong. The correct state of this field is 'the vendor does not publish it', and the note above names the specific document that was read and found not to carry it, so a future pass does not have to re-establish that from scratch.
